current_example.title: Example: Evaluating a Double Integral Using the Additivity Over a Rectangular Domain

q-129935.name: Question 1
q-129935.problem: Which of the following gives the value of the double integral ${∬}_{R}y{x}^{2}{3}^{x+y}\text{ }\text{d}A$ over the rectangle $R=[1,3]\times [0,2]?$
q-129935.worked_solution:
We apply the multiplicative property of double integrals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}y{x}^{2}{3}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}y\,{x}^{2}\,{3}^{x}\,{3}^{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{R}({x}^{2}\,{3}^{x})\text{ }(y\,{3}^{y})\,\text{d}A \\  & =({\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\,{3}^{x}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{2}y\,{3}^{y}\,\text{d}y)\end{aligned}
$$

q-80516.name: Question 2
q-80516.problem: Which of the following gives the value of the double integral ${∬}_{R}{x}^{2}{y}^{3}\text{ }{e}^{2x-y}\,\text{d}A$ over the rectangle $R=[0,1]\times [2,5]?$
q-80516.worked_solution:
We apply the multiplicative property of double integrals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}{x}^{2}{y}^{3}\text{ }{e}^{2x-y}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}({x}^{2}\,{e}^{2x})(\frac{{y}^{3}}{{e}^{y}})\,\text{d}A \\  & =({\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{{y}^{3}}{{e}^{y}}\,\text{d}y)\end{aligned}
$$

q-80517.name: Question 3
q-80517.problem: Which of the following gives the value of the double integral ${∬}_{R}\sqrt{xy}\text{ }\frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}A$ over the rectangle $R=[0,5]\times [3,7]?$
q-80517.worked_solution:
We apply the multiplicative property of double integrals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\sqrt{xy}\text{ }\frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}{x}^{1/2}\,{y}^{1/2}\,{y}^{-1}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{R}({x}^{1/2})\text{ }({y}^{-1/2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =({\int }_{0}^{5}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{3}^{7}\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\,\text{d}y)\end{aligned}
$$

q-71932.name: Question 4
q-71932.problem: Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\text{ }{e}^{y}\,\text{d}A$ over the rectangle $R=[0,\pi ]\times [0,1].$
q-71932.worked_solution:
We apply the multiplicative property of double integrals and then evaluate each of the integrals separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\text{ }{e}^{y}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\text{ }({e}^{y})\,\text{d}A \\  & =({\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =[-\operatorname{cos}⁡x]_{0}^{\pi }\cdot [{e}^{y}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =-(\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\operatorname{cos}⁡0)\cdot ({e}^{1}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =-(-1-1)\cdot (e-1) \\  & =2(e-1)\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(5{x}^{4}+9{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A=2+6=8.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(2-2x+9{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}2\,\text{d}A-{∬}_{R}2x\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{R}9{y}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

The first integral is the double integral of a constant, so we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}2\,\text{d}A & =2{∬}_{R}\text{d}A \\  & =2\text{Area}(R) \\  & =2\cdot (2-0)\cdot (2-(-1)) \\  & =2\cdot 2\cdot 3 \\  & =12\end{aligned}

$$

Finally, combining our results, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(2-2x+9{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A=12-12+54=54.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $C$ and $D$ are finite, non-overlapping regions and that

$$
{∬}_{C}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=\frac{1}{2},\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=\frac{3}{2},
$$

find the value of 

$$
{∬}_{C\cup D}\frac{f(x,y)}{2}\text{ }\text{d}A.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{C\cup D}\frac{f(x,y)}{2}\text{ }\text{d}A & =\frac{1}{2}{∬}_{C\cup D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({∬}_{C}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

Given that C and D are finite, non-overlapping regions and that ∬Cf(x,y) dA=7,∬Df(x,y) dA=1, find the value of ∬C∪D5f(x,y) dA.

a
30
b
35
c
45
d
50
e
40
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the linearity and additivity of double integrals, we get the following:

∬C∪D5f(x,y) dA=5∬C∪Df(x,y) dA=5(∬Cf(x,y) dA+∬Df(x,y) dA)=5(7+1)=40

First, notice that the domain $R$ can be represented as a union of three sub-domains, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =S\cup T\cup U.\end{aligned}

$$

q-80657.name: Question 15
q-80657.problem:
Given that $C$ and $D$ are finite, non-overlapping regions and that

$$
{∬}_{C}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=-5,\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=7,
$$

find the value of 

$$
{∬}_{C\cup D}4f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A.
$$
q-80657.worked_solution:
Using the linearity and additivity of double integrals, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{C\cup D}4f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A & =4{∬}_{C\cup D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A \\  & =4({∬}_{C}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A) \\  & =4(-5+7) \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$
